ID-senate.statusNote: Sen. Jim Risch (R) won the May 19 primary with 67.3% and seeks a fourth term. Democratic nominee David Roth withdrew July 28, leaving independent former state Rep. Todd Achilles as Risch's main challenger.

ID-governor.statusNote: Gov. Brad Little (R) won the May 19 primary with about 59%, defeating seven GOP challengers (Attorney General Raul Labrador was not among them), and seeks a third term against Boise attorney Terri Pickens (D), who won her primary with about 61%.

candidates.name: Jim Risch
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2009 and chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee; rancher and attorney who previously served as Idaho's governor and lieutenant governor. Won the May 19 Republican primary with 67.3% and is seeking a fourth term.
priorities: Extend the 2017 tax cuts and cut federal spending

health.label: Voted against expanding the Affordable Care Act; opposes a larger federal role in health care (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: Says the reconciliation bill he backed 'secures the southern border and provides the money that's needed for immigration enforcement'; opposes a pathway to citizenship (Senate office)

taxes.label: Celebrated his One Big Beautiful Bill vote preserving the 2017 tax cuts, 'the largest tax cuts for working Idahoans in history', while cutting $1.6 trillion in federal spending (Senate office)

climate.label: Touts that the reconciliation bill 'ends the Green New Deal, also known as the Green New Scam' (Senate office)

education.label: Strongly favors vouchers for school choice (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: Favors stricter punishment as a crime deterrent (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Strongly opposes abortion access as a right (Ballotpedia)

nullNotes.housing: checked Ballotpedia and Senate office release, nothing documented
nullNotes.democracy: checked Ballotpedia and Senate office release; he did not join 2020 certification objections but no scoreable voting-rules stance was documented in fetched sources

candidates.name: Todd Achilles
candidates.now: Independent U.S. Senate candidate; former Idaho state representative
candidates.background: Army veteran who deployed to the Persian Gulf, later a technology executive; served in the Idaho House as a Democrat (2024-2025) before leaving the party to run for Senate as an independent. Became Risch's main challenger after Democratic nominee David Roth withdrew July 28; he had outraised Roth roughly $692,000 to $8,600.
priorities: Lower costs through price transparency and anti-price-fixing rules
Term limits and ending congressional stock trading
Give working families a fighting chance

cost.label: Ban pharmaceutical kickbacks to doctors, require 'upfront, itemized prices for procedures and medications', and ban algorithm-driven price fixing (campaign policies)

health.label: Protect health care tax credits and pursue cross-party insurance reforms plus price transparency (campaign policies)

housing.label: Mixed: backs the bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act and supply expansion AND a 'national ban on algorithm-driven price fixing that artificially inflates housing costs' (campaign policies)

immigration.label: Mixed: 'we can secure our border while improving our legal immigration system'; more border staffing plus modernized visas (campaign policies)

taxes.label: 'Lower taxes for working families, small businesses, and ag producers' while closing corporate tax loopholes (campaign policies)

education.label: Protect federal education funding; invest in career and technical education, universities, and research (campaign policies)

repro.label: Supports Idaho's Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act ballot initiative and says voters should decide (campaign policies)

democracy.label: Term limits (two Senate terms, three House terms, 18 years for the Supreme Court), ban gerrymandering, end congressional stock trading (campaign policies)

nullNotes.climate: checked campaign policies page and Wikipedia, no clean-energy versus fossil position documented
nullNotes.safety: checked campaign policies page; only firearm suicide prevention appears, which is a gun item and excluded from this axis by rule

candidates.name: Brad Little
candidates.background: Governor since 2019 and lieutenant governor before that; ran his family's ranching operation for nearly 30 years. Won the May 19 Republican primary with about 59% over Mark Fitzpatrick (29%) and six others, and is seeking a third term on a record of 'lower taxes, reign in government, invest in what matters most.'
priorities: Managing growth: schools, roads, water and housing

cost.label: Frames affordability through 'record tax relief': signed over $400M in 2025 cuts including a $155 per person grocery tax credit (Idaho Capital Sun)

health.label: Signed HB 345 seeking Medicaid work requirements: 'reasonably reeling in Medicaid spending so taxpayers are not overly burdened' (Idaho Capital Sun via Yahoo)

housing.label: Proposed the $50 million Idaho Workforce Housing Fund, state gap financing projected to build about 1,000 units (BoiseDev)

immigration.label: Signed HB 83 creating state crimes of illegal entry and reentry and letting police record immigration status; ACLU sued within hours (Idaho Capital Sun)

taxes.label: Signed HB 40, the largest income tax cut in state history, dropping individual and corporate rates to 5.3% as part of $400M in 2025 relief (Idaho Capital Sun)

education.label: Mixed: signed HB 93 directing $50M to private school tuition tax credits, saying Idaho can 'have it all, strong public schools and education freedom', while conceding 'there's not enough accountability in it' (Idaho Capital Sun)

safety.label: Signed HB 380 allowing the death penalty for child sexual abuse: 'the perpetrators deserve the ultimate punishment' (Idaho Capital Sun)

repro.label: Signed the six-week abortion bans HB 366 (2021) and SB 1309 (2022) and the 2023 'abortion trafficking' law criminalizing helping minors travel for abortions (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Signed HB 124 (2023) removing student IDs from acceptable voter identification (Democracy Docket)

sources.label: Idaho Capital Sun: GOP primary result

nullNotes.climate: checked Wikipedia, the 2025 session recap, and signing coverage; no clean-energy versus fossil position documented in fetched sources

candidates.name: Terri Pickens
candidates.now: Attorney, founding partner of Pickens Law
candidates.background: Boise attorney and founding partner of Pickens Law, raised in Pocatello; the 2022 Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor. Won the May 19 Democratic gubernatorial primary with about 61% over Jill Kirkham (17%), campaigning on public schools and ending what she calls the Legislature's 'endless culture war.'
priorities: Fund public schools: teacher pay, pre-K, full-day kindergarten
An economy for everyday Idahoans, not billionaires

health.label: 'Health care must be affordable and accessible to all Idahoans' (campaign issues)

immigration.label: 'We are a country of immigrants'; wants 'simple and easy ways for them to work here' and opposes demonizing immigrants (campaign issues)

taxes.label: Wants 'a system that works for everyday Idahoans, not billionaires', with a stable tax structure for small business (campaign issues)

education.label: Better school funding, higher teacher salaries, rural district support, pre-K and full-time kindergarten (campaign issues)

repro.label: 'Women have a fundamental right to bodily autonomy'; opposes Idaho's 'dangerous, coercive, and cruel' abortion laws (campaign issues)
